meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Bijural): Quebec private law is civil law (Civil Code of Quebec); federal public law and criminal law follow common law; the province operates within Canada's federal constitutional framework.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CETA (Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement) with the European Union, investment provisions and Investment Court System
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership)
Canada-China FIPA (Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement, in force 1 October 2014)
Canada-Hong Kong Investment Agreement (in force 14 April 2021)
Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (1986) and Canada-US Tax Convention, as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, ss. 354-462.5 and 462.31; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c. 45; Regulations Implementing UN Resolutions on the Suppression of Terrorism, SOR/2001-360; FINTRAC reporting and MSB registration guidelines. Provincial (Quebec): Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 2.6-2.10 and 22-31 (beneficial owner register and enterprise registration); Regulation respecting the application of that Act, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2272 (societe en commandite). Beneficial ownership transparency amendments became effective 31 March 2023, requiring declaration of every individual who directly or indirectly owns 25% or more of the partnership interests or controls the enterprise.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Corporations Canada or the relevant foreign registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for all states party to the 1961 Apostille Convention (in force for Canada as of 11 January 2024); Consular Legalization through the Canadian embassy or consulate for non-convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Directors listing current officers and authorized signatories of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as described above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by the general partner authorizing the Quebec incorporation agent and counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution or a Quebec notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and proof of residential address of each individual partner, including individual general partners and all beneficial owners at or above the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority; utility, bank, or government authority issuing the address proof
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for foreign-issued documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership organizational chart and declaration covering direct and indirect ownership and control of the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec legal counsel in coordination with the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation before a Quebec notary; domestic authentication normally suffices, so no apostille is required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, directors and officers of corporate general partners, and any individual owning or controlling 25% or more of the partnership against: (i) domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) and heads of international organizations as defined in FINTRAC guidance under PCMLTFA; (ii) sanctions lists administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, required because the business routes payments through US-based rails (Apple IAP and Paymentwall); and (v) publicly available adverse media indicators of money laundering, terrorist financing, or fraud. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP interest, for counterparties in FATF-high-risk jurisdictions, or where transactions materially deviate from the declared app-based monetization model. Since Apple IAP and Paymentwall typically act as merchants of record, the LP itself may fall outside the FINTRAC MSB registration threshold; nonetheless, the LP must maintain documented internal controls, a written risk assessment, and a UBO record to satisfy Quebec registry obligations and payment processor due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal - Registre des entreprises - https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Quebec limited partnership must be in French or contain a French version that predminates; the statutory designation 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' must appear in the name. An English or foreign-language brand may be registered as a secondary name if it is a registered trademark or if the French name otherwise predminates, per the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, as amended by Bill 96. All declaration documents submitted to the REQ must be in French or accompanied by a certified French translation; transliteration into Latin script is required for names originally in non-Latin scripts.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Trust, Fiduciaire, Assurance, Insurance (regulated financial terms requiring OSFI, AMF, or ministerial approval)
University, Universite, College (requires Ministry of Higher Education approval)
Cooperative, Coop (requires specific incorporation under cooperative statutes)
Royal, Royale, Canada, Quebec, Government, Gouvernement, Ministere (implies Crown or government connection)
Corporation, Compagnie, Inc., Ltd. (misleading corporate designations for a limited partnership)
Police, Gendarmerie, and terms contrary to public order or containing obscene references
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Renewal: the name reservation may be renewed for an additional 90-day period by filing a new online request and paying the applicable CAD 33 fee before the original reservation expires; otherwise a fresh search and reservation must be filed. Rejection: the REQ issues a written refusal with reasons. The applicant may file an application for administrative review (demande de revision administrative) with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal; if unsuccessful, an appeal lies to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec (TAQ) within 60 days of the review decision, with a further judicial review available before the Superior Court of Quebec. During any appeal, the proposed name is not protected and a parallel reservation should be lodged.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions: under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the head office of a limited partnership may be a non-commercial address (e.g., a registered agency or accounting firm office) located in Quebec, provided the exact physical civic address is disclosed to the REQ. For a digital video-matching platform, however, the general partner must maintain genuine operational substance in Quebec, including a Canadian bank account, contractual records, and a compliance function; Revenu Quebec and FINTRAC may disregard or challenge pure letterbox arrangements for tax residence, permanent establishment, and economic substance purposes, and global payment processors typically require a verifiable physical location before underwriting the merchant relationship.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 15% annual probability of an unannounced verification visit by the Registraire des entreprises or Revenu Quebec during the first two years of operation; probability rises to 25-30% where a virtual office is the sole Quebec presence and the enterprise processes cross-border consumer payments; FINTRAC examination probability is estimated below 5% annually while the LP remains unregistered as an MSB, but increases materially if the LP later handles customer funds directly.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ-1991), arts. 2186, 2236-2250 (societe en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 2-5, 14-20; ancillary application of the Code of Civil Procedure is not required for formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), Division de la publicite legale des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration d'immatriculation (Registration Statement) filed electronically through the REQ CLIP (Centre de liaison informatise) portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Civil Code of Quebec for a societe en commandite; capital contributions are determined exclusively by the limited partnership agreement; no escrow bank account is statutorily mandated for this digital-platform activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the General Partner accepts the capital contribution schedule set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement, and that all limited partners' subscriptions are confirmed as recorded in Schedule A. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office of the Limited Partnership be established at the principal establishment in Quebec, and that all Registraire des entreprises du Quebec filings be executed. RESOLVED FURTHER: That [GP Representative] be appointed General Partner Representative and [Compliance Officer] be appointed Privacy and AML Compliance Officer, each authorized to execute REQ filings, tax registrations, and commercial platform agreements. RESOLVED FINALLY: That the General Partner procure municipal occupational permits, fire safety certifications, and privacy program documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — online enterprise name search and name analysis service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an initial enterprise name search in the REQ public index to confirm linguistic distinctiveness; submit three ranked proposed French-language names with an explanatory note addressing visual and phonetic resemblance to existing registered names. File a name analysis request (optional, approximately CAD 32) with the REQ to obtain a written non-binding opinion on availability before reserving the chosen designation.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name in French (mandatory for Quebec limited partnerships)
Analytical note on distinctiveness of each proposed name
Written consent of the intended general partner to the use of the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or creates confusion, file a statutory amendment to the declaration with the REQ selecting the second-ranked name; re-run the availability search and pay the applicable amendment fee without losing the priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Digital-Commerce Compliance Baseline
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or notary in the province of Quebec (private act or notarial deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Convention de societe en commandite (limited partnership agreement), allocating management exclusively to the general partner, defining capital accounts, profit-sharing ratios, transfer restrictions, and capital calls for application development. Attach a privacy impact assessment aligned with PIPEDA and the Quebec Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, covering video-match data processing and cross-border telephony functions.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (Convention de societe en commandite)
Schedule A — Capital contributions and subscription ledger
PIPEDA and Quebec data protection policies for video-match platform
AML orientation note for Apple IAP and Paymentwall payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Partners may execute an amending agreement to correct capital or governance terms; retroactive clauses are valid among partners provided they do not prejudice third parties' acquired rights.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration (Immatriculation) of the Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — CLIP electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File electronically the Declaration d'immatriculation using the REQ CLIP system, providing the legal name, head office address in Quebec, general partner identifiers, object of the partnership (digital platform, data processing, real-time video matching), first registered office, and unlimited duration. Pay the statutory fee of CAD 78 by debit, credit, or interac; upon approval the REQ issues a confirmation of registration containing the NEQ (Numero d'entreprise du Quebec).
required_dossiers: Complete Declaration d'immatriculation (electronic form)
Power of attorney or authorization of the filing representative
Proof of address of the registered office (lease or notarized attestation)
Extract of the partnership agreement naming the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the REQ requisition within the prescribed response window by filing a correction or completing missing fields; if the filing is rejected and deleted, re-file promptly and pay a new registration fee to avoid interruption of legal publicity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and GST/HST Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ confirmation, access CRA's Business Registration Online portal to obtain a 9-digit Business Number, register for GST/HST, and indicate that the Quebec QST will be administered by Revenu Quebec. Select quarterly electronic reporting, designate an authorized representative, and provide Canadian contact and banking details for remittances.
required_dossiers: NEQ confirmation issued by REQ
Certificate of registration of the limited partnership
General partner identification and representative authority
Bank account domicile and GST/HST remittance jurisdiction information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corrections may be filed electronically through My Business Account; registration completed within 30 days of commencing commercial activity avoids late-filing penalties and preserves the effective date of the tax account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Quebec QST Registration and Enterprise Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec — Mon dossier d'entreprise online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, register for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), the Quebec payroll source deductions account, and contributions to the Quebec Parental Insurance Plan and workforce skills development fund if employees will be engaged. Instruct Revenu Quebec to synchronize GST/HST and QST filing periods on a quarterly basis and to align electronic remittance dates.
required_dossiers: NEQ issued by REQ
GST/HST Business Number confirmation from CRA
Details of anticipated first transaction date for video-match subscriptions
General partner's attestation of commercial activity commencement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If account activation is delayed, contact Revenu Quebec's business client support line; a written service request may be escalated for expedited reply, and retroactive registration is available from the date commercial operations began.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy Permit and Fire Safety Certification for Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local borough permits and inspections service (e.g., Ville de Montreal, Arrondissement) and Regie du batiment du Quebec (RBQ) for fire safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the municipal occupancy permit application for the leased office, providing lease authorization, floor layout showing equipment spaces and exit paths, and compliance with the Quebec Construction Code. Obtain fire safety certification under the Quebec Safety Code, schedule the RBQ or municipal inspector's verification of fire alarm and emergency lighting, post the permit near the entrance, and display the CNESST workplace safety poster before employees begin working on site.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or sublease consent for the registered office
Occupancy permit application (Demande de certificat d'occupation)
Fire safety layout plan and conformity statement to the Code de securite du Quebec
CNESST employer workplace poster acknowledgement (form 500-8486 if hiring)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal a refusal in writing to the borough's inspection committee; for fire protection non-compliance, correct the deficiencies identified by the inspector and obtain a follow-up visit; municipal administrative tribunals provide the final recourse.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporate Register, Privacy Officer Appointment, and Annual Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner's corporate secretary / compliance officer, with filings to REQ and Revenu Quebec as required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish statutory registers including the partners ledger, capital contribution records, and declarations of legal publicity; create the partnership minute book in Quebec; appoint an Information Security and Privacy Officer responsible for PIPEDA and Quebec privacy compliance. Prepare the annual declaration to the REQ before 30 June each year, update the register within 30 days of any change in the general partner or registered office, and implement the governance calendar for ongoing legal publicity obligations.
required_dossiers: Minute book and partnership registers
Register of limited partners and beneficial ownership information
Privacy program documentation and breach-response register
Annual declaration reminder and corporate governance calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any change in registered facts must be reported through an amendment (Modification) to the REQ within 30 days; failure to do so produces a deemed registration and potential penalty, which may be reversed by timely correction and a written request for cancellation of the penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6311 digital-platform activity is not subject to mandatory industrial or manufacturing licensing in Quebec; advisory support may be obtained from the Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE), Direction des entreprises. The over-the-top video-match service operates under the existing CRTC exemption regime for digital media services and does not require a broadcasting or telecommunications license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no statutory operating or manufacturing permit applies; the service operates as an exempt OTT digital-media platform under the Telecommunications Act (Canada) and the Broadcasting Act exemption order for digital media services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the artificial-intelligence video-matching operation generates no industrial discharges, no extraction, and no physical installation; the office-only activity does not trigger an authorization or registration under Section 22 or the REAFIE regulation of the Environment Quality Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater discharge point, no VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste streams are generated; electronic and electrical equipment end-of-life handling must follow the Quebec Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of electrical and electronic equipment, using certified recyclers for any retired ICT hardware.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the RBQ fire safety certification and structural load inspection for the leased office floor in accordance with the Quebec Construction Code; satisfy the CNESST occupational health and safety clearance by adopting a workplace prevention program, posting the mandatory safety notice, and displaying form 500-8486 before commencing operations; annual fire alarm testing and emergency lighting inspection are required for the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), via My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); provincial income/QST collection delegated to Revenu Québec via CLIC portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/CLIC/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership first obtains a CRA business number (BN) and GST/HST account using Business Registration Online. If the LP carries on commercial activity in Québec, it must also register with the Registraire des entreprises for a Quebec Enterprise Identifier (NEQ) and open a QST account with Revenu Québec, either online or by postal filing of the applicable registration forms. Non-resident partners that receive Canadian-source income must obtain or confirm an individual/corporate TIN and, where needed, request tariff/export program account codes (RM) for customs. The LP must maintain a Canadian-recognized agency or access point for service of notices and may appoint a representative in Québec where disclosed partner operations are managed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - a Québec Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax, not a separate taxpayer; income/loss flows to partners. Non-resident partners are taxable in Canada on their share of Canadian-source partnership income (Part I tax, subject to treaty), and to Part XIII withholding where payments are distributions or deemed interest/royalty income. For GST/QST, however, the partnership is treated as a separate registrant/person for supplies made by the partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada; the LP is automatically flow-through. The partners may elect a non-calendar fiscal period under ITA s.249.0.8 if all partners are non-SME and conditions are met. For hybrid mismatch purposes, ITA s.18.4 operates automatically and does not provide a domestic check-the-box election. A limited partnership may make a partnership VAT grouping election under ETA s.273 or the provincial equivalent where conditions are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) imposed on digital supplies; targeted VAT-style simplified registration for foreign digital service providers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or in four consecutive calendar quarters from taxable supplies (including specified digital goods or remote services) to customers in Canada, for a non-resident supplier; a similar CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST registration by remote foreign digital service providers selling to consumers in Québec. Domestic GST/HST general small-supplier threshold remains CAD 30,000 annual worldwide taxable supplies by businesses carrying on taxable activity in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory continuous transaction control, real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. Electronic invoices and records are valid without pre-authorization if all prescribed facts are clearly stated. CRA accepts e-invoices (PDF/XML/EDI) and supports GST/HST NETFILE filing; Revenu Québec accepts QST returns via CLIC. No government API clearance interface is required for issuance, but the supplier must retain audit-quality transaction logs with timestamp, IP geo-location, recipient payment method and bank settlement data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of a service or intangible personal property (including digital real-time video-match/SIP/telephony functionality) is zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST, where the supply is not made in Canada and is not consumed in Canada; if supplied to a person ordinarily resident in Canada or where the location/technical means indicate Canadian use, 14.975% combined tax must be charged. For goods exported from Canada, zero-rating requires actual physical export and documentary proof that the exporter exported, sold and delivered tangible or digital product outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A/B13B) for any tangible media/device carrying the application or cryptographic keys, filed with CBSA.
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or carrier proof from warehouse to final destination outside Canada.
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT MT103/Paymentwall and Apple IAP merchant settlement statements evidencing receipt of export proceeds from non-Canadian counterparties.
Signed zero-rating certificate (GST/HST Status Certificate form) or customer self-declaration confirming non-resident status and foreign consumption.
Detailed invoice and transaction-level logs matching user IP/IMEI/device residency to payment rails, supporting zero-rated treatment.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA/Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating retroactively and assess GST/QST plus default interest if export documentation is incomplete, if the recipient is shown to be in Canada, or if funds receivable are not repatriated and evidenced within the 180-day commercial benchmark. Reassessment can extend beyond the four-year normal period where false documentation or ignorance of facts is established. Knowing, fraudulent or wilful statements in support of zero-rating attract penalties of up to 25% of net federal tax assessed (Excise Tax Act s.280), civil penalties of the greater of $250 and 25% of the GST amount in issue, denial of refund claims, s.239 criminal fines on conviction of up to 200% of evaded tax and up to five years' imprisonment; a promoter or registrant may also be named in the CRA's Voluntary Disclosures or evasion program.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); FX administration and prudential oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); cross-border transaction monitoring and reporting administration by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Currency Act, the Bank Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada has no centralized exchange-control licensing authority; the Bank of Canada manages the floating CAD and maintains the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) / Lynx high-value payment rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible. Canada accepts IMF Article VIII obligations and imposes no restrictions on current or capital account transactions. For the Quebec Limited Partnership (CA_LP) profile: inward capital contributions are unrestricted and free from approval; remittance of operating profits to non-resident partners is not subject to Canadian withholding tax as a distribution, but non-resident partners are taxed under Part I of the Income Tax Act on their allocable share of Canadian-source partnership income and must file Canadian and Quebec (Revenu Québec) returns. Care must be taken to avoid Part XIII withholding on payments characterized as management fees, interest, royalties, or rents payable to non-resident partners. No measurable profit-remittance hurdle exists beyond standard tax filing, transfer-pricing documentation, and FINTRAC reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Canada; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951 and no repatriation or conversion obligation has since been reintroduced. Exporters and service providers may retain foreign currency in offshore or domestic accounts without restriction. FINTRAC requires the reporting of cross-border currency or monetary instrument movements of CAD 10,000 or more and requires regulated financial institutions to record and report international electronic fund transfers (EFTs) of CAD 10,000 or more. GST/HST zero-rating applies to exported services of the video match app; there is no FX surrender mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium (conditional). Canada has no EU-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence; offshore digital EMIs operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) and must register with FINTRAC and, where performing retail payment functions, register under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) administered by the Bank of Canada (regime in force since November 2024). They are legally barred from accepting deposits in Canada unless authorized under the Bank Act. Use of offshore EMIs is viable for operational sub-accounts, multi-currency liquidity pockets, and settlement of Apple IAP / Paymentwall balances, but they are not acceptable as the primary clearing bank or for capital escrow holding. Supporting the medium rating is the enhanced regulatory scrutiny of video chat P2P flows and the absence of CDIC deposit insurance on EMI balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted on a limited basis by certain Schedule I banks via video KYC and certified electronic corporate documents (notably National Bank of Canada and RBC), but for a non-resident, medium-risk Limited Partnership most tier-1 Quebec institutions require at least one authorized signatory, a director of the general partner, or the general partner's representative to attend an in-person interview at a Montreal or Toronto branch. A registered office in Quebec, a Canadian address for service, and a registered agent are typically mandatory. Full remote onboarding is granted only after enhanced due diligence (EDD); in practice, a physical visit is required for any Capital Escrow Account and for all accounts holding third-party (Apple IAP / Paymentwall) settlement proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident multi-tiered LP ownership with opaque beneficial ownership (nominee partners, foreign trusts, or bearer-type structures).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Quebec counsel; notarized Declaration of Registration from the Quebec Enterprise Registrar (Registraire des entreprises); full LP agreement and all amendments; register of partners with ultimate beneficial owner attestations; organizational chart of the general partner; source-of-funds evidence for each capital contributor; and current sanctions / PEP screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-Risk Enhanced classification of a real-time video matching social app with elevated chargeback, fraud, and P2P abuse exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/CTF compliance program; transaction monitoring and fraud prevention procedures; user KYC/KYB verification flow; transaction velocity rules; chargeback management and refund policy; PIPEDA/Quebec Law 25 privacy compliance framework; content moderation and anti-exploitation policy; and audit trail of app-level controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered funds flows via third-party payment aggregators (Apple IAP, Paymentwall) creating merchant-of-record and source-of-funds ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed payment processor agreements; merchant-of-record structure explanation; weekly settlement statements and reconciliation reports; processor-level sanctions screening logs; FINTRAC MSB registration confirmation (where applicable); platform exclusion-list evidence; and independent audit report on settlement flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through entity with no prior Canadian operating history and no Canadian-resident general partner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and financial projections; capital call notices matched to bank credits; GST/HST account registration confirmation; Revenu Québec file confirmation; executed registered agent retainer; office lease or Canadian virtual office agreement; professional letters of reference from Canadian legal counsel and chartered professional accountant; and sworn declaration of the general partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute SWIFT MT103 wires from non-resident partner bank accounts to the LP's Canadian clearing account using the receiving bank's SWIFT/BIC (e.g., National Bank of Canada BNDCCAMMINT). Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'LP capital contribution - no goods/services' and cite a formal capital call notice number; no reference to management fees or royalties should appear to avoid Part XIII characterization. Settlement occurs via Payments Canada Lynx for CAD and Fedwire/CHIPS for USD. Verification protocol: bank must retain the partner subscription agreement, capital-call notice, board/GP resolution, and proof of partner identity; FINTRAC international EFT prescribed records apply at CAD 10,000 and above. No governmental pre-approval is required for inward capital, but banks apply enhanced EDD and may delay the credit until the legal opinion and source of funds (SoF) data are received.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for high-value vendor payments and infrastructure procurement (cloud, bandwidth, content moderation); (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) with ISBP 745 document presentation for large multi-jurisdiction vendor contracts; (3) Canada Lynx for domestic CAD high-value settlements and Fedwire/CHIPS for USD correspondent clearing; (4) Payments Canada Real-Time Rail (RTR) for API-driven low-value recurring disbursements (contractor payouts, moderation incentives); and (5) settlement via Paymentwall or Apple IAP commercial payout APIs for app-store proceeds, with contractual reconciliation of merchant settlement cycles. All outbound remittances must include a purpose code, invoicing evidence, and, where required, an 'On Behalf Of' (OBO) customer identification line compliant with FINTRAC EFT reporting rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (CAD/USD/EUR) executed with an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank under an ISDA 1998 FX Master Agreement
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-clearing currencies (e.g., emerging market pairs) under ISDA/CSA and bilateral bank credit lines
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for long-term CAD/USD treasury and liquidity transformation with OSFI-regulated counterparties
Vanilla FX Options (call/put, physically or cash settled) on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR with bank counterparties
FX Swaps (swap-turned) with maturity under 12 months for rolling short-term treasury positions under master agreements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), administered by Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each registration anniversary date; all registered particulars must be re-certified on each filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty of C$200–C$2,000 for partnerships; continued default, generally after two or more consecutive missed annual declarations, triggers administrative strike-off/deregistration, after which the limited partnership loses juridical standing to operate or enforce its limited liability shield

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and individual T5013 slips for each partner)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the calendar year following the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, due March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of C$25 per partner per day (minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500) for partnerships with more than five partners, or C$10 per partner per day (minimum C$50, maximum C$500) for five or fewer partners; additional penalties of C$100 per missing T5013 slip; general partners remain jointly and severally liable for CRA assessments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return (CO-17) and Relevé 15 (RL-15) partners' information slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CO-17 due by March 31 following the fiscal period end, concurrent with the T5013; RL-15 slips due by the last day of February following the calendar year of income or loss attribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties parallel the federal regime at C$25 per partner per day (maximum C$2,500) for partnerships with more than five partners; RL-15 late-slip penalties of C$100 per slip; interest accrues on any Quebec provincial tax balance, and repeated non-filing may trigger a formal provincial demand and extended audit

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec limited partnership is not statutorily required to obtain an independent external audit unless (i) the limited partnership agreement mandates it, (ii) the partnership qualifies as a reporting issuer under securities legislation, or (iii) CRA or Revenu Québec issues a formal audit demand; given the Medium-Risk AML tier and cross-border IAP/Paymentwall payment rails, an annual independent review or agreed-upon-procedures engagement is strongly recommended
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) or ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II); a private limited partnership typically elects ASPE unless lenders, investors, or the partnership agreement require IFRS; revenue recognition for video-match services and platform fees follows IFRS 15 / ASPE Section 3400 as applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the modernized Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises (S.Q. 2023, c. 19), the limited partnership must maintain accurate declared information and identify all individuals having control, re-certifying these particulars in each annual declaration; any transfer of limited partnership units, change of general partner, or change of registered office must be declared within 30 days of the change, and the annual confirmation updates the public register accordingly; failure to confirm exposes the partnership to administrative deregistration
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions and unit holdings)
Register of General Partners (names, residential addresses, and authority)
Partnership minute book and management committee resolutions (where a control committee operates)
Accounting books and records maintained under Civil Code of Quebec art. 2198 and the Tax Administration Act

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the Quebec LP entity level (fiscally transparent); a taxable Canadian corporation is subject to a combined 26.5% federal/provincial headline rate (15% federal + 11.5% Quebec).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for video-chat social apps in Quebec. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) can access the federal small business deduction (9% effective federal rate) and the Quebec small business deduction (5% effective provincial rate) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; the LP's partners receive allocated income and may qualify for personal/corporate deductions and credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return via CRA My Business Account/E-file; Quebec: TP-600 Partnership Information Return via Revenu Québec Mon dossier d'entreprise.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end must be filed by May 31 of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of LP, business number (BN), Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), registered office, fiscal period end, and responsible general partner contact.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the non-resident partner's Canadian business number, foreign tax identification number, and country of tax residence; no Canadian SIN is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of partnership business income or loss, including revenue from in-app purchases, Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlement amounts, hosting costs, and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate to non-resident partners only the Canadian-source active business income attributable to their partnership interest; foreign-source revenue is separately reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's name, address, SIN/BN, province of residence or country, class of interest, income/deficit allocation, and applicable treaty rate claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach certificates of residency for treaty-reduced withholding; ensure the partner's share of Canadian-source income is on a source-by-source basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-creditable provincial amounts, resource allowances, foreign taxes paid, and non-capital loss allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim treaty domestic income tax credits; do not claim Quebec tax credits unavailable to non-residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal T5013 late filing: CAD 50 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 5,000; Quebec TP-600 late filing: CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500. Knowingly false statements attract the general civil penalty of 50% of the understated tax plus criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII Canadian withholding tax on dividends to non-residents; tax treaties may reduce the rate to 5% (corporate 10%+ shareholder) or 15% (portfolio dividends).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a Quebec LP, a non-resident partner seeking treaty relief must (i) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; (ii) complete CRA Form NR301/NR302 (or applicable treaty claim form) and deliver it to the LP's withholding agent before distributions; (iii) complete Revenu Québec's residency status disclosure (Relevé de renseignements sur le statut de résident) if required; and (iv) report the allocable Canadian-source income and claim the treaty rate on a timely tax return. The LP retains the reduced withholding only after the non-resident certifies beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory Part XIII rate, reduced by treaties to commonly 0% or 10% for copyright and software fees. Interest: 25% statutory rate applies to participating debt interest and certain related-party interest; arm's-length non-participating interest is generally exempt under s.212(1)(b)(vii); treaties typically reduce to 0%–15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate cross-border non-arm's-length transactions triggers mandatory T106/TP-1151 reporting and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; CRA risk-based Local/Master File requests typically arise for transactions exceeding CAD 5,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations in Quebec or Canada. However, the federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Income Tax Act s.245) and Quebec's analogous anti-avoidance rule (Taxation Act s.1079.1) deny tax and treaty benefits where an LP or any partner engages in artificial transactions without genuine commercial substance. The LP must be validly constituted, maintain real activities (e.g., actual video-matching infrastructure and staff), and each partner's rights/duties must be exercised.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of in-app video-chat revenue from Apple IAP/Paymentwall reports, maintaining dual records, claiming fictitious expenses, or failing to remit employee/partner source deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil gross negligence penalty under Income Tax Act s.163(2) of 50% of the understated tax; criminal conviction under s.239 faces a fine of 50%–200% of the tax evaded and up to 5 years' imprisonment; Quebec parallel penalties under the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general partners, and knowingly participating officers are jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions; criminal charges can lead to personal restitution orders, asset freezes, travel bans during prosecution, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file T106/TP-1151, failing to prepare contemporaneous TP documentation, applying a method other than arm's length to revenue-sharing/royalties paid to foreign related video-platform operators, or shifting profits to a non-resident partner in a tax-haven jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing penalty under s.247(4) equal to 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000), plus interest and reassessment; late filing penalties for T106 of up to CAD 5,000; Quebec equivalents under Taxation Act s.1087.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/general partners who knowingly approve false TP studies or misstate income can be assessed gross negligence penalties personally; in cases of fraudulent conduit arrangements, courts may disregard the corporate form and impose personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Quebec LP with no staff, no office, no active video-matching app operations, and artificial routing of Canadian payments to a non-resident to claim tax treaty benefits or avoid Part I tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment (Income Tax Act s.245 / Quebec Taxation Act s.1079.1) denying the treaty and tax benefit, plus interest and a 25% penalty on the tax avoided; Canada's anti-treaty-shopping rules and LOB/PPT provisions disallow undue treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the LP is found to be a sham or fraudulent conduit, the court can pierce the corporate veil and hold the general partner/directors personally liable for unpaid tax and joint tort damages; travel bans and director/professional disqualification orders may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, MSB Registration, and Beneficial Ownership Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a video-chat monetization platform without FINTRAC MSB registration, failing to perform KYC/CDD on merchants/users, not reporting suspicious transactions involving payment charges, or non-filing of Quebec's registre des propriétaires bénévoles (beneficial ownership registry) for the LP's partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; Quebec registry false/omitted declarations subject to fines up to CAD 5,000 and registry cancellation; criminal penalties include imprisonment for obstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and general partners are personally exposed to AML penalties, prohibition orders, and criminal liability where they knowingly aided or failed to prevent money laundering through the payment rails; civil restitution and travel restrictions can accompany criminal AML proceedings.
